title: Best Wardrobe Apps (2026): Digital Closet Apps Compared
h1: The best wardrobe apps in 2026, compared
excerpt: Whering, Indyx, Acloset, Stylebook, Cladwell, Pureple and Get Wardrobe compared on price model, platforms, privacy and outfit tools.
tldr: The best digital wardrobe apps in 2026 balance cataloging speed, outfit planning quality, and privacy. Stylebook is a long-standing iOS-only option. Whering and Acloset offer free starting points on iOS and Android. The right app depends on your platform, privacy requirements, and whether you want AI suggestions.
body:
We compared the publicly listed features of several popular options, based on common criteria: organisation, cost, and data handling.

FitWardrobe is our own app; it isn't available yet, so it isn't ranked here.

FitWardrobe vs the rest
On device

is where FitWardrobe stores your wardrobe. Photos go to a cloud AI service only for tagging and outfit suggestions.

What Makes a Good Wardrobe App?

Before jumping into the comparison, here's what we evaluated:

  • Ease of adding items — How quickly can you photograph and catalogue a garment?
  • AI quality — Does the auto-tagging actually work, or does it call your jeans a "skirt"?
  • Outfit planning — Can it suggest outfits, or is it just a photo gallery?
  • Privacy — Where are your photos stored? Who can access them?
  • Pricing — Free, freemium, or paid? Any hidden costs?
  • Platform — Android, iOS, Web, or all three?
  • Indian relevance — Does it handle ethnic wear categories (kurtas, sarees, lehengas)?

The 7 Apps Compared

Quick Comparison Table

App Platform Pricing model Notable features (from official listings)
Acloset iOS, Android Free for up to 100 items (listed limit, October 2026); paid tiers AI item detection, weather-based outfit ideas, outfit calendar, packing
Pureple iOS (check Google Play for Android) Free with ads; paid plan Outfit ideas from your own closet, background removal
Stylebook iPhone and iPad only One-time purchase Cost-per-wear tracking, outfit calendar, packing checklists, background removal
Indyx iOS, Android, web Free app; paid membership and stylist services Receipt import, human stylists, automatic background removal
Whering iOS, Android Free, with optional paid extras Automatic background removal, daily outfit ideas, cost-per-wear tracking
Cladwell iOS, Android Free plan and paid plan Daily outfit suggestions based on your closet and the weather
Get Wardrobe iOS, Android, web Free for up to 100 items (listed limit, October 2026); paid plan AI outfit ideas from your clothes; paid plan adds packing lists and cost per wear

Features and pricing models are taken from each app's own website or official App Store listing in October 2026. They change often and differ by country, so check the listing before you pay.

1. Acloset

Best for: people who want a feature-rich organiser on iOS or Android

Acloset lets you photograph items, organise them and build outfits. Its official listing describes AI item detection, outfit ideas based on the weather and your schedule, an outfit calendar and packing tools.

Price: Free for up to 100 items (listed limit, October 2026), with paid tiers above that.

2. Pureple

Best for: people who want a free outfit app and don't mind ads

Pureple suggests outfit ideas from the clothes you upload. The free version shows ads; a paid plan removes them and adds unlimited background removal.

Price: Free (ad-supported), with a paid plan. It is listed on the App Store; check Google Play for the Android version.

3. Stylebook

Best for: iPhone users who prefer manual control and a one-time payment

Stylebook is a long-standing wardrobe app for iPhone and iPad, sold as a one-time purchase rather than a subscription. It tracks cost per wear, has an outfit calendar and packing checklists, and includes background removal. Your data is stored on your device and in iCloud if you enable it.

Limits: iOS only, with no Android or web version, and its listing does not advertise AI outfit suggestions.

Price: One-time purchase

4. Indyx

Best for: people willing to pay for human styling

Indyx is a free wardrobe app on iOS, Android and the web with automatic background removal. You can add items by forwarding shopping receipts or pasting product links. It also sells a paid membership, paid sessions with human stylists and, in some areas, a service that digitises your wardrobe for you.

Price: Free app; membership and stylist services cost extra

5. Whering

Best for: people who want a free app with social features

Whering removes photo backgrounds automatically, offers daily outfit ideas, tracks cost per wear and lets you browse friends' wardrobes.

Price: Free to download, with optional paid extras

6. Cladwell

Best for: people who want a daily outfit suggestion

Cladwell suggests outfits each morning from your closet and the weather, and offers capsule wardrobe guidance.

Price: Free plan, plus a paid plan

7. Get Wardrobe

Best for: people who want AI outfit ideas across phone and computer

Get Wardrobe creates outfit ideas from clothes you already own and runs on iOS, Android, macOS and the web. Its paid plan adds unlimited items, packing lists and cost per wear.

Price: Free for up to 100 items (listed limit, October 2026), with a paid plan

Our app (not available yet)

FitWardrobe is the app we are building. It is coming soon on Android and the web and is free during early access. It is not in the list above because you can't use it yet.

When you photograph a garment, a cloud AI service tags its type, colour and season, and you can correct any tag. You can then ask for outfit suggestions for an occasion, built only from clothes you own, each with a short reason. Your wardrobe is stored on your device; the AI features need an internet connection. You can delete your data at any time. There is no iPhone app; iPhone users can use the web version.

Join the early-access list to hear when it opens.

Indyx vs Whering: Which Is Better?

This is one of the most searched comparisons, so let's address it directly.

Choose Indyx if:

  • You want the option of human stylist consultations
  • You shop online a lot and want receipt import
  • You need cross-platform access (iOS, Android, Web)

Choose Whering if:

  • You want a free app with automatic background removal
  • You like daily outfit ideas and cost-per-wear tracking
  • You want to see friends' wardrobes

Consider FitWardrobe (coming soon) instead if:

  • You want your wardrobe stored on your device rather than in a cloud account
  • You want outfit suggestions that each come with a short reason
  • You are happy to wait for an app that is free during early access
  • You're on Android or happy to use a web app

Are Wardrobe Apps Worth It?

Honest answer: it depends on your wardrobe size and how much time you spend deciding what to wear.

Definitely worth it if you:

  • Own a lot of clothes
  • Often struggle to choose an outfit
  • Buy clothes you already own (duplicates)
  • Travel frequently and struggle with packing
  • Want to build a capsule wardrobe but don't know where to start

Probably not worth it if you:

  • Own fewer than 20 items and already know every piece
  • Don't care about outfit planning
  • Are happy with your current wardrobe routine

If a digital wardrobe helps you avoid even a few unneeded purchases a year, that money stays in your pocket. Less daily "what do I wear?" stress is the other possible benefit.

For a deeper analysis, read our Are wardrobe apps worth it? An honest look.

How to Choose the Right App for You

Ask yourself three questions:

  1. What's my platform? Stylebook is iOS only, but Acloset, Whering, Indyx and Cladwell all list Android apps, and FitWardrobe is coming soon on Android and the web.

  2. How much do I care about privacy? If you don't want your wardrobe photos on someone else's server, look for an app that stores your wardrobe on your device. FitWardrobe (coming soon) does this, though photos are sent to a cloud AI service when you ask for tags or suggestions.

  3. What's my budget? If you want a free tool, FitWardrobe will be free during early access, and several other apps have free tiers.

The Right App for the Right User

There is no single best digital wardrobe app — there is the best app for your device, your priorities, and how much time you will realistically invest in it.

For Android and web users who want their wardrobe kept on their device and AI outfit suggestions: FitWardrobe, once it launches. For iOS users who want a one-time purchase and detailed statistics: Stylebook. For a free app on both iOS and Android: Whering.

faq.q: What is the best free wardrobe app?
faq.a: Pureple is free to use but supported by advertising, and Whering, Acloset and Indyx have free tiers. FitWardrobe, our own app, will be free during early access, but it is not available yet.

faq.q: Is the Get Wardrobe app free?
faq.a: Get Wardrobe has a free plan for up to 100 items (listed limit, October 2026). A paid plan adds unlimited items, packing lists and cost per wear.
Pureple is free to use, but it's ad-supported. A paid plan removes the ads.

faq.q: What is an AI wardrobe app?
faq.a: An AI wardrobe app uses artificial intelligence to automatically identify clothing items from photos, suggest outfits, and learn your style preferences. FitWardrobe (coming soon) uses a cloud AI service for these features.

faq.q: Can wardrobe apps help me save money?
faq.a: Yes. By showing you everything you own, wardrobe apps help you avoid buying duplicates and make better use of existing clothes. Fewer impulse purchases can add up to real savings over a year.
